facts.claim: IEC 61082-1:2014 (3rd edition) sets general rules for presenting information in documents plus specific rules for diagrams, drawings and tables in electrotechnology; it replaced the 2006 edition.
facts.note: Also adds presentation rules for wireless interconnections.

facts.claim: The German adoption is DIN EN 61082-1:2015-10 (VDE 0040-1), based on IEC 61082-1:2014; a Berichtigung from 2016-10 exists. No 2025 edition could be found.
IEC 61082-1 is a horizontal standard mainly for technical committees writing their own standards (IEC Guide 108).
facts.note: Secondary listing of IEC scope text.

facts.claim: Practitioner sources describe the document types under DIN EN 61082 as Übersichtsschaltplan (single-line, system structure, e.g. Hausanschluss, Zähler, Verteiler), Stromlaufplan (all-pole, shows functions with all conductors) and Anordnungs-/Installationsplan (position of equipment on a floor plan).
facts.note: Practitioner source, not standard text; wording kept general.

facts.claim: The Stromlaufplan shows a circuit abstractly, not the real arrangement of components, and gives information on how an electrical installation works.
Stromlaufplan exists in zusammenhängender and aufgelöster Darstellung; the zusammenhängende was formerly called Wirkschaltplan, the aufgelöste formerly Stromlaufplan.
facts.note: Terminology from a book index; use as didactic explanation only.

facts.claim: The Verdrahtungsplan shows the conductive connections between electrical equipment; Klemmenplan (terminal diagram) is a separate document type for terminal assignment.
facts.note: Practitioner level; no standard definition of Anschlussplan found.

facts.claim: The Installationsplan shows the position of equipment on a floor plan with symbols, possibly cable routes and circuit numbers.
IEC 81346-1:2022 (Edition 2) sets general principles for structuring systems and rules for unambiguous reference designations; it replaces the 2009 edition and introduces the type aspect.
A reference designation attached to a component is the key to finding information about that object across different documents.

IEC 81346-2:2019 is the current classification of objects with letter codes for classes; German version DIN EN IEC 81346-2:2020-10. The older DIN EN 81346-2:2010-05 is withdrawn. A draft Edition 3 (IEC/DIS 81346-2) is in enquiry.
facts.note: Status of DIS from ISO listing 87205.

facts.claim: Example class letters in EN 81346-2: Q for switching/controlling energy flow (e.g. Schütz, subclass QA), F for protective devices (Sicherung, LS-Schalter), K for processing signals (Relais, Hilfsschütz), M for providing mechanical energy (Motor, subclass MM).
facts.source_name: elekrechner.com Referenztabelle; IHK Region Stuttgart PAL Unterlage zu DIN EN IEC 81346-2:2020-10
facts.note: Secondary sources; not checked against standard text. Present as examples only. Edition 2009 vs 2019 differ in detail.

facts.claim: DIN 6779-2:2004 (older letter codes) is withdrawn; DIN EN 81346-2 is recommended instead.
facts.note: Only the DIN 6779-2 link is verified; DIN 40719 to EN 61346 chain NOT verified.

facts.claim: IEC 60617 is available as the online database IEC 60617 DB (parts 2-13, ~1900 symbols, subscription, searchable, symbols as GIF/DWG/EPS). Edition listings differ (2024/2026), so check the current one.
facts.note: Edition year inconsistent across listings: say 'database' only.

facts.claim: Practitioner sources state symbols follow DIN EN 60617 (formerly DIN 40700) and designations follow DIN EN 81346.
IEC 61355-1:2008 (classification of document kinds) is superseded by IEC 81355-1:2024, which classifies information kinds instead of document kinds.

Terminal marking: current German standard is DIN EN IEC 60445:2023-02 (VDE 0197), based on IEC 60445:2021, on marking of terminals of equipment, conductor ends and conductors; earlier editions withdrawn.
facts.note: Source search says DIN lists it as current.

facts.claim: In manufacturer practice, contactor coil terminals are commonly A1/A2; auxiliary contacts 13-14 (normally open) and 21-22 (normally closed).
facts.source_name: ABB technical document on terminal designations; viox.com

facts.claim: DIN EN 50005 (terminal marking of industrial switchgear, 1977) is withdrawn.
